title: Original Sin
definition: The doctrine of Original Sin teaches that human beings are born into a fallen condition because of Adam’s sin, needing grace before they can make themselves clean.
summary: Original Sin names a real biblical truth, not a religious slogan. human beings are born into a fallen condition because of Adam’s sin, needing grace before they can make themselves clean. It helps believers understand the human condition, God’s promise, and the need to respond to the Lord with honesty and faith.
christFocus: Christ is central to Original Sin because He is the Savior who tells the truth about sin, judgment, weakness, and spiritual darkness while also providing the only lasting hope. In Him, God’s truth does not crush the repentant; it leads them to mercy, cleansing, freedom, and life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: This doctrine focuses on this specific truth: human beings are born into a fallen condition because of Adam’s sin, needing grace before they can make themselves clean. It is not meant to make people feel hopeless; it is meant to make reality plain before God. When this truth is seen clearly, the Bible’s answer in Christ becomes clearer, deeper, and more precious.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because people will mistake sin for only bad choices if they do not see the deeper fallen condition beneath those choices. If this doctrine is blurred, people either minimize what God warns about or carry burdens Christ came to answer. The result is confusion instead of repentance, fear instead of faith, or pride instead of humble dependence on the Lord.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Stop trying to explain sin away as weakness alone. Confess the depth of the problem, then rest in the deeper grace of Christ who saves sinners completely. Keep the language simple when teaching it: name the truth, point to Christ, and show the next faithful step. This helps the wounded, the new believer, the person in recovery, the church-hurt, and the teacher hear doctrine as light from God rather than cold information.
